The [Engine Protocol Reference](upstreamdrift-engine-protocol.html) describes
engine calls. This guide follows the **simulation backend** output: how many
samples a rollout records, which interval each control drives, and what survives
an HDF5 round-trip. Sources and examples are checked against UpstreamDrift
[`2867049f33`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/2867049f33a57637ee766b351538cc8f96e62cd6).

::: {.callout-note title="Scope of the Example"}
The example uses the analytical `ode` backend's planar shoulder–wrist model,
with two angles and two applied joint torques. It does not load a humanoid URDF.
`SimulationBackend` and `PhysicsEngine` are separate interfaces; do not transfer
this model's coordinate counts to a floating-base engine.
:::

## Samples and Controls {#sec-backend-trace-layout}

Let `H = horizon`, `T = H + 1`, and `N` be the batch size. The
[`Trace` and `BatchTrace` definitions](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/2867049f33a57637ee766b351538cc8f96e62cd6/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/protocol.py)
declare these layouts:

| Field | Single `Trace` | `BatchTrace` | Planar Reference Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| `t` | `(T,)` | `(T,)`, shared by all environments | s |
| `q` | `(T, nq)` | `(N, T, nq)` | rad |
| `v` | `(T, nv)` | `(N, T, nv)` | rad/s |
| `u`, when present | `(T, nu)` | `(N, T, nu)` | N·m |
| `dt` | scalar | scalar | s |

The planar `ode` model has `nq = nv = nu = 2`, with
`q = [theta1, theta2]` (shoulder, wrist), `v = [omega1, omega2]`, and
`u = [tau_shoulder, tau_wrist]`, as defined in
[`ode_backend.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/2867049f33a57637ee766b351538cc8f96e62cd6/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/ode_backend.py).
For mixed scalar full-body producers, check the ordered `coordinate_units_json`
and `effort_units_json` metadata instead of assuming every column is rotational.
The `Trace` definition explicitly requires those unit declarations.

`ode.rollout` accepts **`(H, 2)` input controls**, but returns **`(H + 1, 2)`
recorded controls**. Sample zero is the initial state; `u[k]` drives the interval
from sample `k` to `k + 1`. The terminal row is **zero-padded**, since no step
leaves the final sample. It is not an extra zero-torque integration step.
`controls=None` requests a passive rollout and records `u=None`.
Despite its name, `trace.num_steps` counts **samples**, hence `horizon + 1`.

The ODE implementation constructs `trace.t` **relative to the rollout**:
`[0, dt, ..., H*dt]`. It starts from the backend's current state and advances
the live clock. After a nonzero-time reset or a previous rollout, `trace.t[-1]`
therefore need not equal `backend.get_time()`. Reset explicitly for independent
trials; do not concatenate relative time vectors without an offset.

## Run and Save a Controlled Rollout {#sec-backend-trace-example}

Run the following Python blocks in order from an UpstreamDrift checkout at the
revision above, with its Python dependencies and `h5py` installed. All code is
ordinary Python; AffineDrift does not execute it during the site build.
The assertions verify layout and persistence, not cross-engine agreement.

```python
from pathlib import Path

import h5py
import numpy as np

from src.shared.python.simulation_backends import GolfModelParams, SimState, make_backend
from src.shared.python.simulation_backends.trace_io import read_trace, write_trace

backend = make_backend("ode", GolfModelParams.default())
backend.reset(SimState(q=[0.2, -0.1], v=[0.0, 0.0], time=3.0))
H, dt = 4, 0.005
controls = np.tile([0.1, -0.05], (H, 1))
trace = backend.rollout(controls=controls, horizon=H, dt=dt)
assert trace.q.shape == trace.v.shape == trace.u.shape == (H + 1, 2)
np.testing.assert_allclose(trace.t, np.arange(H + 1) * dt)
np.testing.assert_allclose(backend.get_time(), 3.0 + H * dt)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(trace.u[:-1], controls)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(trace.u[-1], [0.0, 0.0])

path = Path("controlled-rollout.h5")
write_trace(trace, path)
restored = read_trace(path)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored.q, trace.q)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored.v, trace.v)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored.u, trace.u)
with h5py.File(path, "r") as saved:
    assert saved.attrs["schema_version"] == "2.1.0"
    assert saved.attrs["kind"] == "single"
    assert saved["u"].shape == (H + 1, 2)
```

[`trace_io.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/2867049f33a57637ee766b351538cc8f96e62cd6/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/trace_io.py)
writes root attributes `schema_version`, `backend`, `dt`, and `kind`, plus
datasets `t`, `q`, `v` and optional `u`. **An existing destination is overwritten.**
Optional histories (`torques`, `wrench`, `markers`, `contacts`, and muscle
outputs) are written only when supplied; an ODE rollout does not populate them.
An absent dataset is not evidence of a measured zero.

Only scalar string, Boolean, integer, and float metadata survive as
`meta_<key>` root attributes. Richer objects are **silently skipped**; encode
structured metadata as a scalar string when the producer's contract requires it.
At this pin the schema is `2.1.0`; the reader accepts major versions 1 and 2,
defaulting missing legacy optional histories to `None`, and rejects other majors.
That compatibility check does not validate a model identity or prove replay parity.

## Inspect a Batch Without a GPU {#sec-backend-batch-example}

[`cpu_batch_rollout`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/2867049f33a57637ee766b351538cc8f96e62cd6/src/shared/python/simulation_backends/batched.py)
constructs a fresh backend per environment and stacks its traces. Here two
identical inputs demonstrate the axis layout, not a performance claim:

```python
from src.shared.python.simulation_backends.batched import cpu_batch_rollout

batch_controls = np.stack([controls, controls])
batch = cpu_batch_rollout(
    lambda index: make_backend("ode", GolfModelParams.default()),
    controls_batch=batch_controls, horizon=H, dt=dt,
)
assert batch.q.shape == batch.v.shape == batch.u.shape == (2, H + 1, 2)
assert batch.num_envs == 2 and batch.num_steps == H + 1
np.testing.assert_array_equal(batch.env(0).u[:-1], controls)
write_trace(batch, "batch-rollouts.h5")
restored_batch = read_trace("batch-rollouts.h5")
assert restored_batch.num_envs == 2
np.testing.assert_array_equal(restored_batch.q, batch.q)
```

`batch.env(i)` extracts one environment as a `Trace`; the environment axis
comes before the time axis. The CPU helper labels the result `cpu-batch`.
Its passive form takes `controls_batch=None` and an explicit `num_envs`.
This example exercises neither CUDA nor differentiable rollout execution.
